Below are five AI-generated responses to the same task, labelled A through E.

Each response was written by one of these five language models:
GPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek.

For each of the five responses, identify which model you believe wrote it, judging only from writing style, structure, and phrasing.

Answer independently for each response. Your five answers do not need to be five different models - name whichever model you believe wrote each response, even if that means naming the same model more than once.

Reply with JSON only, in exactly this form and nothing else:

{
  "A": {"model": "<one of GPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek>", "confidence": <1-5>, "reason": "<one short sentence>"},
  "B": {"model": "...", "confidence": <1-5>, "reason": "..."},
  "C": {"model": "...", "confidence": <1-5>, "reason": "..."},
  "D": {"model": "...", "confidence": <1-5>, "reason": "..."},
  "E": {"model": "...", "confidence": <1-5>, "reason": "..."}
}

confidence: 1 = pure guess, 5 = certain.

--- RESPONSE A ---
Playing board games with family and friends turns ordinary evenings into meaningful experiences because the activity naturally draws everyone into lively conversations and deeper connections as players share strategies, react to unexpected moves, and laugh over memorable moments right there at the table. This shared engagement strengthens bonds in ways that passive activities like watching television simply cannot match, creating lasting memories through direct interaction and mutual enjoyment. Beyond that, the games themselves serve as excellent teachers of good sportsmanship, helping participants learn to celebrate victories humbly while accepting defeats with grace and resilience, skills that carry over into everyday life and foster better relationships overall. 

On top of these social and personal benefits, board games represent an incredibly affordable form of entertainment since a single purchase can provide hours of fun across countless sessions without any recurring expenses, making them far more economical than frequent outings or digital subscriptions that add up quickly. With so many titles offering replayability through varied rules and player dynamics, the investment pays dividends repeatedly, ensuring that time spent around the table remains both enriching and practical for years to come.

--- RESPONSE B ---
Playing board games with family and friends is an excellent way to spend time together, fostering meaningful conversation and connection around the table. In a world often dominated by screens and distractions, board games provide a unique opportunity to engage face-to-face, share stories, and laugh together. Whether it’s strategizing over a competitive game or collaborating to solve a puzzle, these moments create lasting memories and strengthen relationships. The shared experience of playing a game encourages everyone to open up, leading to deeper conversations and a sense of camaraderie that’s hard to replicate in other settings.

Another valuable aspect of board games is the opportunity they provide to teach and practice good sportsmanship. Winning and losing are integral parts of any game, and how we handle these outcomes can be a powerful lesson in humility, grace, and resilience. By playing board games, family and friends learn to celebrate victories without arrogance and accept defeats with dignity. These experiences help build emotional intelligence and character, skills that extend far beyond the game table and into everyday life. It’s a safe and fun environment to teach younger players—and remind older ones—about the importance of fairness, respect, and perseverance.

Finally, board games are an affordable form of entertainment that can be enjoyed repeatedly. Unlike many activities that require ongoing expenses or elaborate setups, a single board game can provide hours of enjoyment for a relatively low cost. Many games are designed with replayability in mind, offering different outcomes each time they’re played. This makes them a sustainable investment in fun and togetherness. Whether it’s a rainy day indoors or a cozy evening with friends, board games offer endless opportunities for enjoyment without breaking the bank, making them a practical and rewarding choice for quality time.

--- RESPONSE C ---
Playing board games with family and friends is time well spent because it gives everyone a reason to sit together, talk, laugh, and pay attention to one another. Unlike watching a show where everyone is facing the same direction, a board game puts people around the same table, reacting to each other in real time. You end up joking, teasing, making plans, telling stories, and sharing little moments that become memories. It is a simple way to turn an ordinary evening into real connection.

Board games also teach good sportsmanship in a natural way. Sometimes you win, sometimes you lose, and sometimes the game changes because of luck or someone else’s clever move. That gives everyone practice being gracious, patient, and fair. Learning to celebrate someone else’s win, handle disappointment, and keep the mood friendly is valuable for kids and adults alike. It reminds people that the point is not just victory, but enjoying the time together.

They are also one of the cheapest forms of entertainment you can keep enjoying again and again. Once you own a game, you can play it many times without buying tickets, paying for food out, or spending money every time you want to have fun. A single game can bring hours of entertainment across many nights, with different outcomes and different laughs each time. For something so affordable, board games offer a lot: conversation, connection, life lessons, and repeated fun with the people who matter.

--- RESPONSE D ---
Listen, I know your evenings fill up fast and the easy thing is to collapse on the couch and scroll until you fall asleep, but hear me out on this one. Pulling out a board game with your family or a few friends is one of the best uses of a free hour or two that I can think of, and I think if you tried it more often you'd come to agree. There's something about sitting across a table from the people you care about, with a board and some pieces between you, that opens up a kind of connection you just can't manufacture any other way. You talk. You tease each other about questionable strategies. Old stories come up out of nowhere, inside jokes get recycled, and somewhere between turns you end up actually learning what's going on in each other's lives. No one is half-watching a screen or waiting for a notification. Everyone is right there, in the same moment, and that shared attention is rarer than it used to be and more valuable because of it.

Beyond the conversation, playing games is quietly one of the best ways to practice being a decent human being in miniature. Every game has winners and losers, and how you handle both says a lot about you. Sitting down regularly to play teaches you, and especially teaches kids, how to lose gracefully when the dice don't cooperate, how to win without rubbing anyone's nose in it, how to follow rules you didn't make, and how to be patient while someone else takes their turn. Those are small lessons on any given night, but they add up, and they transfer out into the rest of life in ways you don't always notice until later. A family that plays together learns how to disagree, compete, and still like each other at the end of the evening, which is a skill a lot of adults never quite master.

And then there's the simple practical argument, which is that board games are an absurdly good deal. A movie night out for a family of four these days can run you a small fortune once you add up tickets and snacks, and it's over in two hours with nothing to show for it. A good board game might cost you twenty or thirty dollars once, and you can play it dozens, even hundreds of times. The cost per hour of entertainment drops to almost nothing, and unlike most purchases it tends to appreciate in sentimental value the more you use it. The worn corners and the handwritten house rules on the inside of the lid become part of the fun. So the next time someone suggests pulling a game off the shelf, say yes. It's cheaper than going out, better for your relationships than another streaming binge, and quietly good for your character on top of it. That's a hard combination to beat.

--- RESPONSE E ---
I was thinking about how we should plan our next get-together, and I really think we should set up a board game night. In a world where everyone is constantly glued to their phones or distracted by screens, sitting down around a table to play a game is one of the best ways to truly connect with the people you care about. Unlike watching a movie where everyone sits in silence, a board game naturally sparks conversation, laughter, and playful banter. It gives us a shared focus and a reason to talk, tell stories, and interact in a way that we rarely get to do in our busy daily lives, strengthening our relationships with every roll of the dice.

Beyond just the social connection, playing board games is a fantastic, low-stakes way to practice and teach good sportsmanship. Whether you are playing with kids or just among competitive adults, games create a safe environment to experience both the thrill of victory and the sting of defeat. Learning to congratulate a winner graciously and accept a loss with a smile is a valuable life skill that translates far beyond the game board. It teaches us patience, resilience, and how to enjoy the process of playing rather than just focusing on the end result, which ultimately makes us better friends and family members.

Finally, from a purely practical standpoint, board games are incredibly cheap entertainment that you can enjoy over and over again. While a night out at the movies, a concert, or a fancy dinner can easily drain your wallet in just a few hours, a single board game is a one-time investment that provides endless hours of fun. You can pull the same game off the shelf years down the road, and because every playthrough is different depending on who is playing and what strategies are used, it never gets old. It is an affordable, sustainable way to make lasting memories, and I really hope you will join me at the table for our first game night very soon.

--- END OF RESPONSES ---
Now output the JSON object described above, and nothing else.
